content: Rotavirus is a leading cause of diarrheal illness, hospitalizations, and deaths globally. The World Health Organization (WHO) has prequalified four vaccines for rotavirus: Rotarix (GlaxoSmithKline), RotaTeq (Merck), Rotasiil (Serum Institute of India Ltd), and Rotavac (Bharat Biotech Ltd). These vaccines have been evaluated for their efficacy and safety in children through randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Rotarix Infants vaccinated and followed for the first year of life: In countries with low child mortality, Rotarix prevented 93% of severe rotavirus diarrhea cases and 52% of severe all-cause diarrhea cases. The evidence for rotavirus diarrhea prevention is of high certainty, while for all-cause diarrhea, it is of moderate certainty. In medium-mortality countries, Rotarix prevented 79% of severe rotavirus diarrhea cases and 36% of severe all-cause diarrhea cases, both supported by high-certainty evidence. In high-mortality countries, Rotarix prevented 58% of severe rotavirus diarrhea cases and 27% of severe all-cause diarrhea cases, with high-certainty evidence for both outcomes. Infants vaccinated and followed for two years: In low-mortality countries, Rotarix prevented 90% of severe rotavirus diarrhea cases and 51% of severe all-cause diarrhea episodes. The evidence for rotavirus diarrhea prevention is of high certainty, while for all-cause diarrhea, it is of moderate certainty. In medium-mortality countries, Rotarix prevented 77% of severe rotavirus diarrhea cases and 26% of severe all-cause diarrhea cases, with high-certainty and moderate-certainty evidence, respectively. In high-mortality countries, Rotarix prevented 35% of severe rotavirus diarrhea cases and 17% of severe all-cause diarrhea cases. The evidence for rotavirus diarrhea prevention is of moderate certainty, while for all-cause diarrhea, it is of high certainty. RotaTeq Infants vaccinated and followed for the first year of life: In low-mortality countries, RotaTeq prevented 97% of severe rotavirus diarrhea cases, supported by high-certainty evidence. In medium-mortality countries, RotaTeq prevented 79% of severe rotavirus diarrhea cases, but the evidence is of low certainty. In high-mortality countries, RotaTeq prevented 57% of severe rotavirus diarrhea cases, with high-certainty evidence. However, there was little to no difference in severe all-cause diarrhea cases compared to placebo, based on moderate-certainty evidence. Infants vaccinated and followed for two years: In low-mortality countries, RotaTeq prevented 96% of severe rotavirus diarrhea cases, supported by high-certainty evidence. In medium-mortality countries, RotaTeq prevented 79% of severe rotavirus diarrhea cases, but the evidence is of low certainty. In high-mortality countries, RotaTeq prevented 44% of severe rotavirus diarrhea cases and 15% of severe all-cause diarrhea cases, both supported by high-certainty evidence. No studies reported on severe all-cause diarrhea in lowor medium-mortality countries. Rotasiil Infants vaccinated and followed for the first year of life: In high-mortality countries, Rotasiil prevented 48% of severe rotavirus diarrhea cases, with high-certainty evidence. However, there was little to no difference in severe all-cause diarrhea cases, also supported by high-certainty evidence. Infants vaccinated and followed for two years: In high-mortality countries, Rotasiil prevented 44% of severe rotavirus diarrhea cases, with high-certainty evidence. There was little to no difference in severe all-cause diarrhea cases, also supported by high-certainty evidence. Rotasiil has not been evaluated in RCTs conducted in lowor medium-mortality countries. Rotavac Infants vaccinated and followed for the first year of life: In high-mortality countries, Rotavac prevented 57% of severe rotavirus diarrhea cases and 16% of severe all-cause diarrhea cases, both supported by moderate-certainty evidence. Infants vaccinated and followed for two years: In high-mortality countries, Rotavac prevented 54% of severe rotavirus diarrhea cases, with moderate-certainty evidence. No studies reported on severe all-cause diarrhea at two years of follow-up. Rotavac has not been evaluated in RCTs conducted in lowor medium-mortality countries. Safety None of the four vaccines (Rotarix, RotaTeq, Rotasiil, or Rotavac) were associated with an increased risk of serious adverse events (SAEs). This conclusion is based on high-certainty evidence for Rotarix and Rotasiil, and moderateto high-certainty evidence for RotaTeq and Rotavac. Deaths were infrequent, and there was insufficient evidence to determine the effect of these vaccines on all-cause mortality. Intussusception, a rare adverse event, was not found to occur at increased rates with any of the vaccines. Conclusions All four WHO-prequalified rotavirus vaccines (Rotarix, RotaTeq, Rotasiil, and Rotavac) effectively prevent episodes of rotavirus diarrhea. The relative efficacy of these vaccines is lower in high-mortality countries compared to low-mortality countries, but the absolute number of cases prevented is higher in high-mortality settings due to the greater baseline risk. In high-mortality countries, vaccine efficacy appears to decline in the second year of life. None of the vaccines were associated with an increased risk of serious adverse events, including intussusception.
